papers.notes: This paper describes the pathophysiology of inflammatory joint diseases like osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis by analyzing synovial fluid, but it does not evaluate any specific treatment or care.

This review discusses the therapeutic potential of electroactive biomaterials to suppress inflammation and promote bone repair in conditions like osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis, supporting the concept of effective inflammatory care.
This review presents umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and their secretome as a promising therapeutic approach for treating arthritic joints by counteracting the inflammatory environment.

This review highlights umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells as a promising treatment for cartilage diseases like osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis due to their anti-inflammatory and regenerative properties.
This article focuses on research models for arthritic pain and explicitly states that conditions like osteoarthritis remain poorly treated, which does not support the efficacy of current care.
This review describes autologous protein solution (APS) as a promising biological treatment for early-stage osteoarthritis due to its concentration of anti-inflammatory mediators.
This study investigates a potential infectious cause of rheumatic symptoms and does not discuss or evaluate any treatments for joint inflammation.
This study identifies a potential inflammatory biomarker in dogs with osteoarthritis and is not relevant to the efficacy of treatments or care.

papers.notes: This review on mesenchymal stem cell therapy for canine osteoarthritis reports a tendency to improve lameness and joint pain, though it also calls for more research to confirm efficacy.
This randomized, placebo-controlled trial found that a specific joint supplement significantly improved mobility and quality of life in dogs with osteoarthritis.
This narrative review on mechanical osteoarthritis suggests that conservative management, including nutraceuticals, is less effective as it does not address the underlying altered joint mechanics.

This study investigates a gene therapy for a specific inherited joint disease (MPS I) in dogs, which is not representative of common joint discomfort, and found that the treatment's efficacy declined over time.
This randomized controlled trial demonstrated that a targeted macrophage-modulating therapy (EF-M2) achieved clinically meaningful pain relief and functional gains in dogs with osteoarthritis.
This clinical study found that both platelet-rich plasma and allogeneic adipose-derived stem cell injections were effective in reducing chronic pain in dogs with degenerative hip joint disease.
